page.layout: One page of running text, one column, with marginal notes in the margins; the printed page number "3" with asterisks sits at the foot. Running head at top: "PHILOSOPHIÆ."

main_text.p: scientia est, sed eius rei, quæ per se semper est, aut sæpissime, tefte eodem Philosopho in x. metaphysicorū libro. Eius autē rei, quæ seper est, scientia metaphysica dicitur: alterius physica, quoniā subiestū eius huiusmodi est. Quare hæc reuera scietia est, non autem ea quæ dicitur, nec quæ, quoniam operibus & fine multum inter se discrepant, etsi versatur in eodē subiecto, quod quidem naturale corpus est, & mutabile. Cæterum ea ex parte tempus, reliquaque naturæ accidentia Physicus meditatur ac cognoscit, qua ipsum tempus est motus affectio, & ipse motus magnitudinis perfectæ. page.notes: Greek words in the second and third lines of the body are printed as: "θεωρητικὴ" (theoretica) and "ποιητικὴ" (poetica), the printed Greek is partly damaged; the glyphs after "dicitur" and "quæ" are read as ἀπὸ/ποιητικὴ-type Greek and marked as doubtful. Marginal "PHILOSOPHIÆ." running head read from the scan. Lines near the start of the page show faint smudging; "scientia" at the top is the continuation of a sentence from the previous page. The printed text reads "semper est, aut sæpissime" with "sæpissime" in the scan as "sępissime"; the vowel is doubtful. Possible printing error: "aut sæpissime, tefte eodem" (the word "tefte" is printed as "teste" in the scan with a reversed form, read as "teste").
